nodes.content: Design distributed incremental view maintenance preserving snapshot-consistent outer joins and aggregates across retractions, partition failures, and concurrent transactions.
requirements: Match full recomputation at every committed snapshot across 100,000 transactions, including crash recovery.
Maintain atomic multi-table updates without globally pausing writers or rescanning unaffected base-table partitions.

nodes.content: Use MVCC durable replayable transaction bundles, per-key outer-join match counts, signed aggregate deltas, and atomic commit-watermark publication after shard acknowledgments.
How are multi-shard retractions kept invisible until every affected shard durably acknowledges a transaction, even across failover?
Replicated commit barriers over shard-durable prepares yield zero partially visible retractions across 100,000 crash-injected transactions.
Stage per-shard MVCC deltas, replicate prepare acknowledgments and commit decisions, then advance the visibility watermark; replay decisions after failover.
Implement staged MVCC deltas, replicated prepare/decision logs, commit-watermark barriers, and failover replay; crash-inject 100,000 transactions, checking partial visibility.
T100K observed zero partially visible retractions across 100,000 transactions and 1,204 injected shard failovers.
Adopt replicated prepare/decision barriers for atomic visibility, given T100K’s zero partial retractions across 1,204 failovers.
CommitBarrier v1 implements shard-local staged MVCC deltas, replicated transaction decisions, visibility watermarks, and idempotent failover replay.
Stress-test adopted CommitBarrier v1 with 100,000 concurrent retraction transactions and leader-transfer crashes; count partially visible snapshots.
LeaderTransfer100K observed 7 partially visible snapshots across 100,000 transactions when failover reused unfenced prepare acknowledgments.
Epoch-fenced prepare acknowledgments and recovery-validated commit barriers should eliminate partial snapshots during 100,000 leader-transfer transactions.
Fence stale prepare acknowledgments by epoch; recover transactions from replicated decisions, verifying every participant’s durable prepare before advancing watermarks.
Patch CommitBarrier v1 with epoch-fenced acknowledgments and recovery prepare checks; rerun LeaderTransfer100K, counting partially visible snapshots.
LeaderTransfer100K still found 2 partial snapshots: recovery advanced watermarks before lagging shards replayed prepared deltas.
Extend CommitBarrier v1 recovery to await every participant’s replay-applied acknowledgment before publishing watermarks; rerun LeaderTransfer100K against full recomputation.
LeaderTransfer100K found zero partial snapshots and zero full-recomputation mismatches after requiring replay-applied acknowledgments from every participant.
Epoch-fenced prepare acknowledgments and per-participant replay-applied acknowledgments before watermark publication yield zero partial snapshots across 100,000 leader-transfer transactions.
Integrate epoch fencing and replay-applied barriers into CommitBarrier v2; verify full-recomputation equality and unaffected-partition writer progress.
Upgrade CommitBarrier v1 with epoch-fenced prepares and replay-applied barriers; test 100,000 leader-transfer transactions against recomputation and unaffected-partition writer throughput.
CommitBarrier v2 matched recomputation at all 100,000 snapshots with zero partial snapshots; unaffected-partition writers sustained 98% baseline throughput.
CommitBarrier v2 adds epoch-fenced prepare records, per-participant replay-applied acknowledgments, and watermark publication gated on all participant acknowledgments.
Run EpochStorm100K on CommitBarrier v2 with overlapping leader transfers during replay; count partial reads and recomputation mismatches.
EpochStorm100K found 3 partially visible snapshots: replay-applied acknowledgments from superseded epochs satisfied newer barriers during overlapping leader transfers.
Use transaction-digest-bound, generation-fenced apply certificates before snapshot publication, with per-key outer-join counts and signed aggregate deltas.
How can publication reject superseded replay acknowledgments when leaders transfer repeatedly during a transaction’s recovery?
Bind apply certificates to transaction digest and shard generation; regenerate after failover, publishing only with each shard’s current-generation certificate.
Implement digest-bound, generation-fenced apply certificates; run EpochStorm100K with overlapping failovers, comparing outer joins and aggregates against recomputation.
EpochStorm100K recorded zero partial snapshots and zero recomputation mismatches; untouched partitions required no rescans.
ApplyCert v1 provides transaction-digest-bound, generation-fenced shard certificates and a publication gate verifying all current-generation participants.
Use partitioned MVCC lineage indexes and per-key differential joins to reconcile null-extended rows and aggregates before certified snapshot publication.
How can per-key lineage prevent duplicate null-extended rows when concurrent retractions and inserts change join matches within one snapshot?
Transaction-coalesced per-row match counts emit null-extension deltas only on zero-crossings, yielding zero recomputation mismatches across 100,000 snapshots.
Implement partitioned lineage and transaction-coalesced match-count zero-crossings under ApplyCert v1; compare joins and aggregates against 100,000 recomputed snapshots.
Lineage100K matched all 100,000 recomputed snapshots, but index recovery rescanned 12 unaffected base-table partitions after shard failures.
Replay only affected-key lineage WAL records under ApplyCert v1 after shard crashes; compare null-extension zero-crossings against recomputation across 100,000 snapshots.
LineageReplay100K showed 4 recomputation mismatches: duplicated WAL replay emitted null extensions twice after crash recovery.
Durable per-key lineage checkpoints and transaction-row-ID-deduplicated WAL replay should yield zero recomputation mismatches and unaffected-partition rescans across 100,000 snapshots.
Checkpoint match counts and applied transaction-row IDs atomically; replay affected-key WAL suffixes idempotently, then emit zero-crossing deltas once.
Add atomic per-key lineage checkpoints and transaction-row-ID replay deduplication under ApplyCert v1; rerun LineageReplay100K with crash injection.
LineageReplay100K found zero recomputation mismatches across 100,000 snapshots and zero unaffected-partition rescans after 600 shard crashes.
LineageStore v2 atomically checkpoints per-key match counts and applied transaction-row IDs, replaying only affected-key WAL suffixes.
Adopt LineageStore v2: checkpointed deduplicated replay eliminates the four duplicate-delta mismatches and twelve unaffected-partition rescans.
Maintain MVCC per-group SUM/COUNT and counted MIN/MAX trees from LineageStore v2 deltas; publish transaction-wide versions via ApplyCert v1.
How can MIN/MAX replace retracted extrema without scanning unaffected partitions or exposing partially updated aggregate groups?
Update per-group counted B-trees with coalesced signed deltas; stage replacement extrema under MVCC and publish after ApplyCert validation.
Integrate LineageStore v2 deltas with MVCC counted extrema trees; crash-test 100,000 retractions against recomputation and unaffected-partition scan counts.
Extrema100K matched full recomputation at every snapshot; MIN/MAX replacement scanned zero unaffected partitions across 500 crashes.
AggIndex v1 stores MVCC SUM/COUNT and counted MIN/MAX B-trees per group, consuming transaction-coalesced LineageStore v2 deltas.
Stress AggIndex v1 with 100,000 concurrent cross-shard group moves and leader failovers; compare every published aggregate to recomputation.
GroupMove100K found 6 aggregate mismatches: ApplyCert v1 certified lineage writes before asynchronous AggIndex v1 source-group deletions applied.
Retain counted extrema trees, but require aggregate-apply certificates before publication; GroupMove100K exposed six mismatches despite Extrema100K’s success.
Gate each transaction’s snapshot on generation-fenced certificates covering both lineage replay and all affected aggregate-group updates.
How can publication prove cross-shard source-group deletions and destination-group inserts are both applied after concurrent failovers?
Digest-bound certificates listing affected lineage keys and aggregate groups should eliminate GroupMove100K mismatches when verified at current shard generations.
Extend ApplyCert certificates to cover AggIndex v1 source and destination groups; rerun GroupMove100K with overlapping shard failovers.
GroupMove100K recorded zero aggregate mismatches across 100,000 snapshots; source and destination group certificates survived 800 overlapping failovers.
Run Oscillate100K with AggIndex v1, repeated cross-shard group moves and late failover replay; compare certified snapshots to recomputation.
Oscillate100K found 5 recomputation mismatches after late replay overwrote certified aggregate versions; GroupMove100K retained zero mismatches.
Retain group-complete certificates, but require monotonic aggregate-version fencing: GroupMove100K passed, while late replay caused five Oscillate100K mismatches.
Generation-fenced, group-complete certificates plus per-group monotonic MVCC version fencing should yield zero Oscillate100K mismatches despite late replay.
Persist each group’s last applied transaction version; reject stale replay writes before issuing group-complete certificates and advancing snapshot watermarks.
Add monotonic group-version fencing to AggIndex v1; rerun GroupMove100K, checking generation-current certificates and source/destination aggregates against recomputation.
GroupMove100K again matched recomputation at all 100,000 snapshots, with zero missing source or destination group certificates.
Run Oscillate100K on fenced AggIndex v1 with late replay and overlapping failovers; verify current-generation certificates and every snapshot’s aggregates.
Oscillate100K: zero mismatches on 40,000 GroupMove100K-equivalent snapshots, but two after repeated moves despite current-generation certificates and version fencing.
Instrument AggIndex v1’s two Oscillate100K failures; replay their cross-shard group moves and compare fenced versions with certified snapshots.
Both Oscillate100K failures restored stale group-version fences from checkpoints; replay with durable fences matched recomputation.
Persist group-version fences atomically with AggIndex v1 checkpoints; run GroupMove100K to verify certificate completeness and recomputation equality.
GroupMove100K found one mismatch: a current-generation, digest-complete certificate attested a staged source-group deletion before durable application.
Retain group-complete certificates, but issue only after durable aggregate application and atomic fence checkpoints; earlier passes missed both defects.
